messages:
maria: Quick FYI — ran an apples-to-apples compare between model-v1-int8 (kernel=A) and model-v1-fp16 (kernel=B) using the replay harness + identical prompts/decoding params. Seeing a consistent 6–9% latency delta favoring kernel=A when KV is warm, but it flips to ~10% regression for kernel=A on cold-KV paths. Any ideas?
aj: can you paste the harness command + config? was it replay or synthetic?
maria: replay. command:
```
./harness/replay_run.py --model model-v1-int8 --prompts ./tests/1000_prompts.json --decode '{"temp":0.0,"max_tokens":64,"stop":["\n\n"]}' --batch 8 --warm_kv 1 --profile
```
config: batch=8, continuous_batching=true, kv_prefetch=true
tom: did you ensure tokenizer alignment? tokenization differences can change per-token counts and affect batching.
maria: good call — I used the upstream tokenizer by default. Token counts we observed:
- model-v1-int8: avg_tokens=38
- model-v1-fp16: avg_tokens=41
elena: aha that's a likely confound. Even with identical input+decode, different tokenizer files produce different encodings. Pin the tokenizer and normalize. Quick check: 
```
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizers/model-v1.json'); print(t.encode('Hello').ids)"
```
aj: also double-check stop-seq handling — we had one model trimming the stop token earlier which changed output length and affected cost.
maria: re-ran with pinned tokenizer + explicit stop handling. Tokens now match avg 39/39. Warm-KV numbers: kernel=A median p50=22.8ms p95=58.1ms; kernel=B p50=24.2ms p95=61.9ms.
tom: what's cold-KV scenario look like?
maria: cold-KV (kv_prefetch=false): kernel=A p50=31.4ms p95=89.6ms; kernel=B p50=29.6ms p95=83.2ms — so kernel A regresses more on cold.
kevin: do we have profiler stacks / nvprof traces?
maria: attached a short summarized profiler snippet from gpu_profiler:
```
Kernel A: softmax+flash_attn fused: 42% time, KV_load 18%, other 40%
Kernel B: attention split: matmul 55%, KV_load 10%, other 35%
```
elena: that implies kernel A spends more relative time in KV_load on cold paths or doesn't overlap KV loads with compute effectively. Batch overlap may not hide I/O.
aj: try changing batching heuristic: bump batch to 16 and widen the continuous batching sample window (20ms) so we can aggregate more small requests.
maria: ran batch=16: warm-KV both improved and gap shrank (p50 A=27.1ms B=27.9ms). Cold-KV still worse for A.
tom: can we replicate with synthetic load (Poisson) instead of replay? replay can have weird session locality.
maria: synthetic run with synth_load.py (rps=120, jitter=0.1) results:
- kernel A p50=25.9ms p95=63.3ms
- kernel B p50=26.7ms p95=66.0ms
This matches warm replay. Seems replay has longer inter-session gaps causing KV eviction.
aj: hypothesis: replay traces include long gaps between requests for some sessions which cause KV eviction/TTL; the harness should optionally group session requests closer to emulate production locality.
kevin: propose adding a KV warmup pre-pass: pre-seed KV for session IDs that will be replayed within a short window (200ms).
maria: agree. Also need more detailed NVPROF traces for hot vs cold runs to see exact memcpy/PCIe stalls. Filed infra ticket: https://redwood/infra/issue/INF-1245 :eyes: 
ci-bot: load-test job #487 finished — artifacts at https://ci.redwood/tests/487 (profiles + logs)
elena: next steps: 1) standardize tokenizer & stop-seq in bench harness 2) add kv-warmup mode for replay 3) run batch heuristic sweep (8/16/32 + sampling window 5/10/20ms) 4) collect nvprof traces for representative cold regressions
maria: I'll run kv-warmup + batch sweep tomorrow and post results. Thanks :thumbsup: 
tom: saved raw perf csvs to /perf/results/2063456789/ — use for dashboard comparisons.
kevin: cc @platform-team for potential kernel-selection policy tweak (prefer kernel B for cold-KV workloads).
